Yes - IF there's substantial warming and IF there's substantial polar ice melt, then sea levels will rise, coastal communities will be flooded and weather patterns will change. But along with that, formerly inland (and underdeveloped) land will be the new coast land, formerly arid land will get increased rainfall and become fertile, formerly inhospitably cold areas will get milder weather and so on. The effects will actually be global and complex, and it's safe to assume that when it all settles out, the worldwide situation won't be much removed from what it is right now. There'll still be coasts and areas with low rainfall and areas with high rainfall and warm areas and cool areas and so on - their arrangement will undoubtedly just change a bit. So?
